headline: High: Plandex can write/execute against shared project files while Authelia exposes broad network/OAuth surfaces, creating default-risk leakage and workflow corruption pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no browser or subprocess execution, so it is not a strong injection source. B reads and writes the project directory and can process stdin/stdout, so if Authelia outputs are manually copied into Plandex or placed in shared files, prompt-like content could steer B. The bridge is indirect and unusual, so low fits.
conditions: IF Authelia outputs are copied into Plandex prompts or files
IF Plandex treats shared file content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep Authelia outputs out of shared project files
Use a separate review-only folder for copied text
Prefix imported text as untrusted data
Disable auto-apply when ingesting external content

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read and write the project directory and send data to a model provider or Plandex Cloud, while A has broad network egress and OAuth/OIDC surfaces. Even though A touches no explicit sensitive data class, the pair can move file contents and auth-related material across boundaries in default workflows. The interaction is plausible from docs, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF the shared project directory contains secrets or tokens
IF Plandex sends file contents to a remote model provider or cloud backend
mitigations: Exclude secrets from the project directory
Use self-hosted or local-only model endpoints
Review files before planning runs
Rotate any credentials stored in shared paths

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and spawn_subprocesses; A exposes network/OAuth-facing services but no local write surface. The pair can still conflict on shared mutable project state if Authelia-generated artifacts are edited by Plandex in the same workspace. Because the shared-dir assumption is not explicit, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same working tree or mounted directory
IF Plandex auto-applies changes while Authelia-related files are being updated
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Require manual git review before apply
Lock the repository during plan execution
Run Plandex in review-only mode

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a planner that stages and optionally auto-applies changes, so if it consumes Authelia-derived outputs as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect code or config changes. A can emit network/OAuth-related outputs, but there is no direct verification bridge documented. The pathway exists in default planning workflows, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Plandex uses Authelia-generated text as source-of-truth input
IF auto-apply is enabled or review is skipped
mitigations: Require human verification of Authelia-derived claims
Keep auto-apply disabled
Add a checklist for source attribution
Compare generated diffs against original inputs

E_compliance.rationale: A is an authentication service with broad network/OIDC surfaces, while B is a coding tool that handles source code and model-provider keys. No explicit residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, and A touches no listed sensitive data class. The main issue is a generic compliance gap around auth logs and code artifacts, so low is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated credentials or personal data are stored in the shared workspace
IF logs from either agent are retained beyond policy
mitigations: Avoid storing regulated data in shared paths
Set short log-retention windows
Review access controls on model-provider keys
Document data-handling boundaries
